podcast.body: This song, Abba's only number one hit in 1976, is lauded by Tim Jones (The Guardian, 2016) as "the best pop song ever" for its catchy melody, blend of influences (Elton John, The Beatles, Bee Gees/disco), and great first line. Pete Waterman highlighted how Swedish artists "soak up popular trends and regurgitate them as something fresh" through songs like this. Tom Bryan of Stereo Gum noted that its success hinges on the full emotional commitment of singers Lyngstad and Fältskog, portraying the massive, all-consuming importance of a night in a nightclub for a 17-year-old. "Tom Bryan, who writes the stereo gum number one series, is as enthusiastic about Dancing Queen as Tim Jones. He said Dancing Queen only works, if Lingstad and Foltzguck put everything into the song. You can't be neutral with Dancing Queen. You have to belt it and you have to put feeling into it."
